name: Qatar
summary: A peninsula ruled by the Al Thani family; British protectorate (1916–71); natural gas made it one of the richest countries; hosted the 2022 World Cup.

location.value: The Qatar Peninsula on the northeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, surrounded by the Persian Gulf except for its land border with Saudi Arabia.

climate.value: Very hot summers (often 40 °C), mild winters and only about 70 mm of rain a year.

resources.value: The world's third-largest natural gas reserves, plus oil.

population.value: About 3.18 million, of whom about 3.02 million are foreign expatriates and migrant workers.

urbanisation.value: The capital, Doha, is home to over 80% of the people.

migration.value: Migrant workers make up most of the population; their treatment has been criticised as amounting to forced labour.

economicBase.value: Natural gas: one of the world's largest exporters of liquefied natural gas.

tradeRoutes.value: Ras Laffan Port is the world's largest liquid natural gas export facility.

wealth.value: The fourth-highest GDP (PPP) per capita in the world.

moneyAndTax.value: No income tax, giving one of the lowest tax rates in the world.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: Officially a constitutional hereditary monarchy, but widely described as an absolute monarchy: the emir holds nearly all power.

keyRulers.value: Qatar is ruled by the hereditary emirs of the Al Thani family; individual emirs are not named here.

succession.value: A hereditary monarchy of the House of Thani since 1868.

institutions.value: The Shura Council, appointed by the emir; a partial election in 2021 was abolished in 2024.

eliteConflict.value: In 1995 the crown prince seized power from his father, the then emir.

armyAndTech.value: Al Udeid Air Base, forward headquarters of US Central Command, houses about 10,000 US military personnel.

alliancesRivals.value: In June 2017 Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Egypt and Yemen cut ties with Qatar; the crisis ended with the al-Ula declaration in January 2021.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: The Doha Metro links key parts of the capital, including Hamad International Airport.

languageWriting.value: Arabic is official, with Qatari Arabic the local dialect; English is common as a second language.

artsArchitecture.value: Museums such as the Museum of Islamic Art, opened in 2008.

socialStructure.value: A small citizen population; foreign workers form the large majority, and women are only a quarter of the population.

sharedIdentity.value: Qatar National Day (18 December) remembers Jassim bin Mohammed Al Thani's unification of the tribes and builds national identity.

neighbours.value: Saudi Arabia (its only land border); Bahrain across the Gulf of Bahrain; the United Arab Emirates nearby.

ideasReligions.value: A mediator in Middle Eastern conflicts since the 2000s.

colonisation.value: Under Ottoman rule from 1871, then a British protectorate (1916–1971).

riseSignals.value: Independence in 1971, when the special treaty arrangements with the United Kingdom ended on 3 September.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
